newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares record losses, ITC takes a beating.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares record losses, ITC takes a beating.

text.p: ** - Indian stocks end down, dull undertone
** Major players keen sellers in pivotals, traders say
** ITC stock takes a battering, slides nearly 4 percent
** Benchmark Bombay share index falls 55.85 points or 1.77
percent to 3,092.72, off 3,143.89 - the day's high
** National stock exchange index loses 1.82 pct, Delhi
index 1.5 pct, Calcutta 1.34 pct and Madras 3.64 pct
Share prices fell across major Indian stock exchanges on Monday with major players hesitant to take postions in the market, dealers said.
The key 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) lost 55.85 points, or 1.77 percent, to close at 3092.72 while the National Stock Exchange index fell 16.55 points to 890.13
"Trading was very dull. There is hardly any action in the market," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities.
Shares of tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd declined 11.75 rupees or 3.92 percent to 287.25, with sellers dominating action in the counter, traders said.

Last week, India's Enforcement Directorate searched the firm's offices and arrested senior officials including two former chairmen in a widening investigation in a foreign exchange scandal which was "to the tune of over $100 million," according to the Finance Ministry.
The directorate, the watchdog over issues related to corporate finances, is investigating alleged violations of foreign exchange rules by India's biggest cigarette maker.
The ITC stock has plunged nearly 10 percent on the BSE since news of the scandal broke out, thus reflecting market fears over the company's future, analysts said.
UBS Securities in a note to investors reiterated its sell recommendation on ITC. "The risks in the stock have still to crystallise," said UBS analyst Sandeep Bhatia.
Auto-component maker Sundram Fasteners said its first-half net profit ending September 30, 1996 rose 28 percent to 193.0 million rupees compared to its year-ago period.
Sundram announced its results after close of market hours.
SBI lost 8.75 rupees to 218.50 rupees, TISCO 5.0 to 171.75, Reliance 5.75 to 188.75, ACC 52.20 to 1,456.0, Bajaj Auto 20.70 to 927.75, MTNL 4.50 to 221.75 and M&M 6.25 to 309.25.
